Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team found the streaming and routing demo useful. We'd like to lock in a hands-on onramp lab / load-sprint next week so we can validate throughput and p95 latency on our key flows and exercise routing fallbacks. High-level ask: a 2-hour workshop with a short kickoff (20 min), prompt/playbook review (30 min), and a 60–70 minute load window where your team runs a managed throughput run while we replay traffic.

Goals / targets from our side:
- Throughput: ~500 concurrent virtual users (peak), ~8k tokens/sec sustained for 10m
- Latency SLO: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 400ms for short prompts (~64 tokens)
- Verify prefix caching and routing behaviour for sharded traffic

Availability: Dec 18–20 during US PST business hours. Can you confirm if you can provide the test harness + a slot to upload our prompt set? Also copy our procurement address so we can attach any necessary NDAs/PO paperwork.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick technical notes to support Naomi’s plan.

- Harness: we’ll ship a small python harness that opens N parallel async connections and drives prompts according to the user-id mapping you provide. It emits per-call token counts and timestamps to the dashboard.
- Routing/playbook: if you want to exercise model fallbacks, include a small set of prompts labeled with "route:heavy" so we can force the fallback path in the policy.
- KV cache: to validate prefix reuse, include 20% repeated prefixes in the prompt set.
- Observability: we’ll stream metrics to the shared Grafana + provide p50/p95 time series and a CSV export.

From an infra standpoint, if you’re aiming for sustained 8k tokens/sec we’ll:
- Use a dedicated 8xA100 bench pool, with batching cap set to 64 tokens and a max concurrent requests setting of 600
- Enable continuous batching and an aggressive KV reuse window

I’ve attached poc-runbook-v2.pdf (runbook checklist + commands) and added a short snippet below for the harness command: 

  python3 runner.py --prompts s3://acme-onramp/prompts.jsonl --concurrency 600 --tokens-per-batch 64 --out metrics.csv

If the team wants to run preliminary dry-run earlier, I can spin up the bench pool for a 30-min rehearsal.

— Dylan
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc-runbook-v2.pdf
